correctness.rationale: Exact trace expansion for the five-cycle gives A Σx²+B Σadj x_jx_{j+1}, independent of complex phases, because tr W⁴=0. On the simplex, Fourier eigenvalues of I+(q/2)Adj(C5) are 1+q cos(2πk/5). They yield uniqueness and the precise nullspace family up through γ=√5−1. Above γ, explicit zero-sum negative-curvature directions on supports of sizes 5 and 4 eliminate those supports; enumeration of both induced three-vertex support types yields the exact (2+q)/(6+q) value and unique three-support profiles. At q=2, direct completion of squares yields the full continuum of degenerate minimizers. The proof covers q∈[0,2], all phases and boundary weights. The 7059 finite checks supplement, not certify, continuous assertions.

value.rationale: The sharp constant and complete optimizer geometry are natural for fixed-energy cyclic shift matrices under a parameterized Schatten numerical radius, not arbitrary parameter slicing. The unique uniform optimum becomes an entire two-dimensional family at the golden-ratio Fourier threshold, then jumps to exactly three-support optimizers, followed by a rigorously classified endpoint continuum. The critical phenomenon structurally differs from the nonzero winding of 4-cycles and boundary paths; exact constants and all equality cases are mathematically meaningful even without a broader theorem.
